topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: Answer these questions about famous American criminals.
question.text: This criminal was able to break out of what was said to be an "escape-proof" jail in 1934. He and his namesake gang terrorized the Midwest, allegedly robbing 24 banks and four police stations.
question.clue: A raid on this man at the Little Bohemia Lodge in Wisconsin turned into a full-on gunfight, during which Helen Gillis, the wife of his associate "Baby Face" Nelson, was captured.

swap.leadin: This is the common name for the Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance program.
swap.text: What federal program provides income to millions of retired people?
swap.clue: The Supreme Court case Flemming v. Nestor established that Congress can revise and amend this policy, which was expanded to include disability in 1954.

question.leadin: Name some organizations established during the New Deal.
question.text: This largest New Deal agency was created by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and provided jobs and income to the unemployed; it also operated large arts, media, and literacy projects.
question.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

swap.text: This 31 st president was largely blamed for the Great Depression, and disgruntled citizens set up makeshift shantytowns sarcastically nicknamed after him.
swap.clue: As Secretary of Commerce, this politician responded to the Great Mississippi Flood, which boosted his popularity prior to an election in which this politician's party declared "a chicken in every pot."

question.leadin: Crucial parts of it were rejected by the Supreme Court in 1936, since it forced farmers to limit production.
question.text: Name this New Deal act which subsidized farmers for their idle land so as to raise crop prices.
question.clue: This bill from the New Deal aimed to raise the price of crops by paying farmers subsidies to kill excess livestock and leave a portion of their land unfarmed, which would prevent crop surplus. A namesake agency was created to manage it.

swap.text: The AFL scored a major victory in 1935 with the passage of the Wagner Act, which set up this independent government agency to resolve labor disputes.
swap.clue: The act that created this organization has since been notably amended by the Landrum-Griffin Act as well as by a piece of legislation that outlawed closed shops and allowed for an emergency presidential injunction, the Taft-Hartley Act.

question.leadin: This pilot was deemed "an American girl of the right type" by Amy Guest, who sponsored her 1928 transatlantic flight.
question.text: Name this American, who disappeared with copilot Fred Noonan while trying to circumnavigate the globe in 1937.
question.clue: A small museum is dedicated to this woman in Derry, Ireland.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the founder of the Fifth Party System.
swap.text: One of the major contributors to the New Deal was this member of the Brain Trust, who was the first director of the New York City Planning Commission and later governed Puerto Rico.
swap.clue: In another role, this man was influenced by the ideas of Clarence Perry and Clarence Stein in trying to design three thousand self-sufficient communities while working with John Lansill, those communities being known as Greenbelt Towns.

question.text: The Communist Party tried to bribe Victoria Price to change her testimony against this group, defended by Samuel Leibowitz. For 15 points, Powell v. Alabama overturned some convictions of what group of nine black youths falsely charged with rape?
question.clue: James Horton presided over a trial of this group for the "god fearing people of Decatur County;" in that trial, Samuel Leibowitz defended them for the American Communist Party.

swap.text: Its namesake act was signed into law by Hoover in June of 1930. It arrived at its rates by adopting Senate rates on farm products and House rates on manufactures. Hurting foreign trade when other countries responded with tariffs of their own, it merely prolonged the Great Depression. For 15 points-name this tarriff, the highest in American history.
swap.answerHtml: Smoot-Hawley tariff [or Hawley-Smoot tariff; or Tariff Act of 1930; prompt on Tariff Act]
swap.clue: Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 as a direct Democratic response to this Republican legislation.

question.leadin: Note to Players: A description is acceptable for the first part. Handwriting analysis helped convict Bruno Hauptmann for the kidnapping of this person.
question.text: Name or describe this child whose 1932 kidnapping and murder led to a "Trial of the Century" and the passage of the Federal Kidnapping Act.
question.answerHtml: Charles Augustus Lindbergh Jr. [accept answers describing Charles Lindbergh’s son, accept the Lindbergh baby]

swap.text: One possible cause of the Great Depression may have been the large tax cuts proposed by this man, Hoover's Secretary of the Treasury. He had previously served in the same position under Harding and Coolidge and had become extremely wealthy working in Pittsburgh industries.
swap.clue: Those proceedings occurred after this man financially backed Pittsburgh-based members of Cox's Army.

question.leadin: This man warned that if Congress did not support Franklin Roosevelt, there would be a "revolution that makes the French Revolution look silly."
question.text: Name this "radio priest" who then went on to oppose FDR. He was based out of the National Shrine of the Little Flower in Detroit.
question.clue: This man established the National Shrine of the Little Flower Basilica in Royal Oak, Michigan.

swap.text: This supervisor of the WPA was one of Roosevelt's closest advisors and served as Secretary of Commerce for Roosevelt near the end of his second term. He served as FDR's primary emissary to Britain during WWII and oversaw the lend lease program.
swap.clue: The phrase "Arsenal of Democracy" was suggested by this advisor to FDR, who crafted the WPA and was integral in implementing the Lend Lease Program.

question.leadin: Identify the following pieces of legislation from the first half of the twentieth century.
question.text: An amendment to Section 2 of the Clayton Antitrust Act, it made it illegal to sell goods at different prices to distributors in order to reduce competition.
question.clue: In 1936, Congress passed this law to outlaw price discrimination that might give large retail chains an advantage over independent stores.

swap.text: As Hennepin County Attorney, Olson filed a public nuisance injunction against the antisemitic Saturday Press, leading to this Supreme Court case that found prior restraint of the newspaper in violation of the First Amendment.
swap.clue: As Chief Justice, Hughes wrote the majority opinion in this 1931 case supporting freedom of the press. This case struck down a Minnesota law targeting "scandalous" newspapers.

question.leadin: Answer the following about union busting in America in 1937.
question.text: The Memorial Day Massacre during the 1937 Little Steel strike was investigated by this Senate Committee on labor rights, which was chaired by the son of a third-party presidential candidate who ran with Burton K. Wheeler.
question.answerHtml: La Follette Committee [or La Follette Civil Liberties Committee] (It was chaired by “Young Bob,” the son of Robert M. La Follette.)

swap.leadin: One law of this name set up agricultural experiment stations which were later expanded via the Smith-Lever Act.
swap.text: Identify this legislation which shares its name with a 1939 "Act to Prevent Pernicious Political Activities" which effectively barred federal employees from engaging in political campaigns.
swap.clue: A more famous bill of this name was co-sponsored by Morris Sheppard and Warren Austin and was upheld in the Supreme Court case of United Public Workers v. Mitchell, over a sharp dissent by Hugo Black on First Amendment grounds.

question.leadin: Name some details of Great Depression-era photographs.
question.text: A portrait of Allie May Burroughs was taken in by this photographer, who documented rural Alabama through staying with the Burroughs, Fields, and Tingle families. He compiled his photos into the collection Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.
question.clue: This photographer took pictures for the Farm Security Administration, documenting the Great Depression in Southern states, particularly Alabama. He collaborated with James Agee on Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.

swap.leadin: Tom McCoy was a principal actor in this event, which in the span of a single day used the favorable results of a recount to reorganize the entire government of Rhode Island.
swap.text: Identify this pivotal event of Rhode Island history which took place on January 1, 1935, and in which a possible case of voter fraud allowed Democrats to assume complete control of state politics.
